newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares close down in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares close down in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian shares closed a litle lower on Monday in quiet trade despite higher prices for some of the market leaders.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index slipped 0.27 points to close at 234.02 on moderate turnover of 16.88 million pounds ($4.96 million).

Broker Youssef Khalil of Delta Stockbrokers said many investors were on the sidelines as they awaited the next privatisation offers -- another milling company this week, with many other shares to follow in early September.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development, the most active stock, closed 1.25 up at 116.00 pounds but flour mill shares, the recent focus of the market, ended mixed.
North Cairo Flour Mills fell to 93.50 from 93.95 despite unconfirmed reports that its 1995/6 profits would be 82 to 84 million pounds, a hefty 13.80 pounds per share.
"The shares are probably due for another rise," said broker Sherif Cararah of Financial Brokerage Group.
Central Egypt Flour Mills rose to 24.50 from 24.33 on expectations of good profits, brokers said.
Commercial International Bank (CIB) rose 5.01 to close at 455.01 pounds. "There has been some arbritrage on the GDRs but I believe the gap has now closed," said Cararah.
The broker said few investors were liquidating their assets to buy new issues because they had learnt from experience that with massive oversubscription their allocations would be small.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to a 17-month high of 338.57 from 335.91 points on Sunday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 160.00 from 161.13.
